label: Antizionism
scope: the post is about antizionism as a concept: defining it, naming it as a distinct ideology or hatred, distinguishing it from antisemitism or from criticism of Israel, offering a framework for recognizing it, or debating the terminology. Not for posts that merely involve antizionism

label: Jewish antizionism
scope: the post focuses on Jews or Jewish organizations promoting antizionism (e.g. Jewish Voice for Peace, IfNotNow, individual anti-Zionist Jewish figures): their arguments, influence, history, or responses to them

label: History of antizionism
scope: the post traces how antizionism originated or developed over time (any era or region), not one that only cites a historical precedent

label: Jew-hatred
scope: the post places antizionism within the longer history of Jew-hatred (e.g. anti-Judaism, then antisemitism, then antizionism) or analyzes Jew-hatred as one phenomenon across its forms

label: Yevsektsiya
scope: the post discusses the Yevsektsiya (the Jewish sections of the Soviet Communist Party) and its campaign against Zionism or Jewish life, beyond a passing mention

label: Arab/Nazi antizionism
scope: the post examines collaboration or ideological transmission between Nazi Germany and Arab or Muslim leaders (e.g. Amin al-Husseini), or Nazi propaganda against Zionism aimed at the Arab world

label: Western antizionism
scope: the post examines modern antizionism in the West and the ideas it draws on (e.g. third-worldism, anti-imperialism, postmodernism, postcolonial or decolonial theory), not one that only reports antizionist incidents in a Western country

label: Institutional capture
scope: the post examines how antizionism has become embedded in an institution's policies, leadership, staffing, funding, or curricula (e.g. universities, NGOs, professional bodies, unions, government agencies)

label: Red/Green alliance
scope: the post examines cooperation or ideological convergence between the far left and Islamist movements
